body.limit: At this recommendation the 1Gbps link is saturated and the locked UDP flow offers 2Gbps; the sender-side scheduler gives each flow a part of the link, so TCP is capped near half the link at 482007923 bps, and the tested queue lengths and TCP types stay at or below that share (E1,E2,E3,E4,E6,E7,C1,C4,C5,C6,C7,C8,V1,V4,V5,V6,V7,V8).
body.explanation: With the default FIFO or plain CoDel, UDP fills the sender queue and TCP never gets sustained ACKs, giving 0 bps (E0,E4,E5). Replacing the sender queue with a scheduler or FQ-CoDel isolates flows, lets TCP establish, and yields about 482 Mbps (E1,E4). The scheduler/FQ-CoDel service then caps TCP near its fair share: q250 and TcpBic match q100 Cubic within tolerance, q4 and q1000 are lower, and BBR is much lower (E2,E3). FQ-CoDel reaches the same goodput with lower RTT and inflight, and its extra retransmissions match the extra total drops, while CoDel q1000 only lets a few TCP probes survive (E4,E5,E6,E7,T20,T21,T22,T25,T26,T29,T30,C11,V11). Scheduler q100 Cubic is preferred because it ties the maximum observed TCP goodput with fewer retransmissions than FQ-CoDel or Bic and a shorter queue than q250; expected values are tcp_goodput_bps=482007923, udp_goodput_bps=489526240, and tcp_retrans=71.

claims.text: Per-flow isolation is required for TCP to deliver data under the locked 2Gbps UDP flow.
The best TCP goodput observed is 482007923 bps with scheduler or FQ-CoDel at l1.queue.length=100 and TcpCubic.
Queue length and loss-based TCP type do not raise scheduler TCP goodput beyond 1%: q250 and TcpBic match q100 Cubic, while q4, q1000, and BBR do not exceed it.
The cap is fair service on the saturated link: UDP and TCP each receive about half the 1Gbps link, and FQ-CoDel's lower inflight tracks its lower RTT at identical TCP goodput.
FQ-CoDel's 6100 retransmissions versus scheduler's 71 at identical goodput are explained by extra TCP drops, not a larger TCP share; CoDel q1000's small 1158 bps is only occasional probe survival.
